summary: The verifier compares the complete report (every README key, both list orders, exact status/flags/ids, tenth-exact TWA or null, dose to 1e-6 relative/absolute) against sealed expectations for every named HC-4 rule. Each rule has an isolating fixture whose outcome changes when the rule is wrong, and the rules the manual leaves open are pinned by shipped-package differentials. I recomputed the sampled expectations by hand from the manual and they are correct. I found no accepted wrong implementation and no rejected contract-valid one.

files_read: tests/shipped/app/** (10 files; identical SHA-256 to the environment/app copies per packet-manifest.json:15-24,52-61, so they were read through those copies)
unread_or_truncated_ranges: task.toml is not in this packet: the sound_verifier packet withholds metadata by design (packet-manifest.json:65-69). No check on this axis depends on it.

tests/expected/limits_workers.jsonl, limits_logs.jsonl and generated.jsonl are single long lines. Read truncated them, so I extracted them with Grep instead. I read every survey input and every report row and group row in limits_workers and generated, and every report row and group row in limits_logs. I read the L-2880 and L-PEAKS logs in full; for the 1,500-run L-1500 log and the middle of the 500-peak list I checked only the first and last segments. That data is bulk limit-reaching input: its section-1 bounds are enforced mechanically by within_limits and load (tests/test_outputs.py:136-175), and no soundness check depends on the individual elements.

checks_performed: Mapped every rule in the manual (1.2, 2.2-2.6, 3.1-3.3, 4.1, 5.1-5.3, 6.1), plus the README ordering and key rules, to the test and fixture that isolates it (tests/test_outputs.py:225-331).

Static hand recomputation from the manual formulas (not an execution): HC4-0001 A4/A6; HC4-0002 B1/B2/B3; HC4-0003 A1/A2; HC4-0004 B2; HC4-0005 A1/A2; HC4-0006 B1/B2; HC4-0007 A1; HC4-0008 B1/B2; HC4-0009 A1/A2; HC4-0010 B1/B2/B3; HC4-0012 B1/B2; HC4-0013 A1/A3; HC4-0014 B2; HC4-0015 X1/X2; HC4-0016 Y1/Y2/Y4/Y5; HC4-0017 group G1; HC4-0018 group G1; HC4-0019 Y1; HC4-0020 Z1/Z2; HC4-0021 A1; HC4-0023 A3/A4; HC4-0024 R0/R1; HC4-0025 T0-T3; HC4-0026 group G1; HC4-0037 V1/V2; HC4-0031 L-2880/L-PEAKS; HC4-0032 GD6H5. Every expected value agreed with the manual.

Walked plausible wrong implementations through the fixtures: 90/5 criterion, >80 threshold, sampled time from counted runs only, 40.0 excluded from readings, paused runs in sampled time, projection to 480, projection of surveys below three quarters to the worker's own shift, no projection at all, scaling down surveys longer than the shift, above-ceiling runs counted at their own level, ceiling flag at >=115, impulse at >140, federal TWA formula, floor rounding, status on the unrounded TWA, >=85 treated as over, group TWA as the mean of member TWAs, quiet or null members dropped from the group mean, group status inheriting member flags, wrong group order. Each is rejected by at least one exact comparison.

Contract-valid alternatives: comparisons parse JSON and ignore extra keys (tests/test_outputs.py:184-204); int or float numbers are accepted for dose and twa; key order and whitespace do not matter; the dose tolerance is 1e-6 relative or absolute, against expectations given to about 12 significant digits.

Checked whether an exact half of a tenth can be reached. Levels have one decimal and lengths are integers, so every dose lies in the Q-span of 2^(2j/60). A TWA at x.x5 needs a dose of 100*2^(n/60) with n odd, which is linearly independent of that span, so an exact half cannot occur and half-up versus half-even cannot change a graded result.

Differential harness: the shipped package's equality check is self-consistent for every pair. The pairs vary only the shift (below three quarters, measured nothing) or an above-ceiling level against 115.0, so the candidate must reproduce today's kept step.

Harness: the driver is replaced before any candidate run and its bytes are checked afterwards; candidate code runs as UID 65534 under python3 -I -S from a neutral path; test.sh runs chmod -R a+rX /app so the candidate package stays readable.

coverage_sweep.category: Map each required behavior to an assertion that fails if it is missing or reversed
coverage_sweep.reason: One test per rule. Each family compares the whole report of every survey (compare at tests/test_outputs.py:197-204). For every rule in the manual I found a fixture whose expected output changes when that rule is reversed.

coverage_sweep.category: Full core result checked, not only existence, keys or row count
coverage_sweep.reason: Every README key is compared: dose numerically, twa to the tenth or as null, survey/id/group/status/ceiling/impulse by exact type and value. Row counts and order are enforced for both lists.

coverage_sweep.category: Isolating case for each named domain rule
coverage_sweep.reason: 3.1: HC4-0001 single-level shifts. 2.3: HC4-0003 A1 at 80.0 vs A3 at 80.1 vs A2 at 79.9. 2.4: HC4-0006 B2 (479 min at 40.0). 2.2: HC4-0007 A1. 3.3 own shift: HC4-0010 B2 (shift 360). 3.3 longer than the shift: HC4-0011 A1 and L-2880. 2.5 at exactly three quarters: HC4-0013/0014, e.g. 458 of 610 against 457 of 610 in HC4-0016. 5.1: HC4-0021. 5.2: HC4-0022 139.9 vs 140.0. 4.1: HC4-0023. 1.2: HC4-0024 (floor vs nearest). 5.3: HC4-0025 S1-S4 and T0-T3. 6.1: HC4-0026 (mean of doses vs mean of TWAs) and HC4-0027/0028 (quiet members). The README group order is checked by HC4-0029.

Every wrong variant I traced produces a different dose, twa, status, flag or order on at least one fixture; see checks_performed. The unmodified shipped package fails on essentially every family (90/5 criterion, >80 threshold, floor rounding, TWA-mean groups).

coverage_sweep.category: Contract-valid alternatives accepted (formatting, ordering, implementation choices)
coverage_sweep.reason: Output is parsed as JSON, extra keys are ignored, int or float is accepted, and the tolerances cover float-summation order. Rounding at an exact half cannot occur (see checks_performed). For the figures the manual leaves open, the instruction fixes today's step computed from the manual's sampled and measured figures, so no alternative is contract-valid there.

coverage_sweep.category: Documented restrictions and lifecycle (driver byte-identity, figures left to today's code, open inputs)
coverage_sweep.reason: Driver byte-identity is checked before and after all runs, both in pytest and in test.sh. The kept steps (projection below three quarters, dose of nought when nothing was measured, above-ceiling counted level) are pinned by family expectations and by the shipped differential. The open inputs from the instruction are excluded from every fixture by within_limits.

coverage_sweep.category: Stale binaries, self-controlled comparisons, oracle-specific representation
coverage_sweep.reason: Expectations are sealed JSONL whose SHA-256 values are pinned in ROSTER. The shipped differential copy is verifier-owned (UID 65533, mode 700). The candidate cannot supply the expected side, and nothing compiled can go stale. Comparisons are semantic, not byte-level.

coverage_sweep.category: Reachability of graded cases within the section 1 domain
coverage_sweep.reason: load() asserts that every graded survey stays within the section 1.4 limits and carries only the inputs its family is declared to hold, so no graded case lies outside the contract.

coverage_sweep.category: Signed derived quantity partitions (TWA above and below the criterion) and state initialization
coverage_sweep.reason: TWAs both above and below 85 are graded (for example 53.3, 71.3, 81.9, 85.0, 115.0), and a dose of zero is graded as null. The only state is a per-worker accumulation over runs, with no initialization-sensitive transition beyond an empty log, which HC4-0017 grades.
